messages:
Alex Chen: hey team — customer reported weird embedding dims intermittently. their app expects 1024 but sometimes gets 1536. ticket #C-4521. they say it started after we pushed a model variant last week.
Maya Patel: thanks alex. are the mismatches correlating with any specific endpoint or auth key?
Alex Chen: looks like all calls to /v1/embeddings with their api_key. sample call they made: 
```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-XXX\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"open-embed-2\",\"input\":[\"hello world\"], \"prefix\":\"project-123\"}'
```
Kevin O'Reilly: curious about that `prefix` field — cache key construction changed a bit in the last deploy. might be related.
support-bot: Incident detector: deploy at 2024-10-02T03:04:21Z touched cache key schema (embed-cache).
Maya Patel: do we include model id & quantization in cache key?
Kevin O'Reilly: we used to include full model id, quant, and seq len. last patch removed `model` from key when `prefix` provided to save space. rationale: prefix should namespace. but if customers reuse same prefix across different model families it can collide.
Alex Chen: the customer says they pass a stable prefix (project-123) and sometimes get 1024, sometimes 1536. could be two model variants (open-embed-1 = 1024, open-embed-2 = 1536) being cached under same key.
SRE Oncall: logs for that api_key around 1772003600 - 1772004600 show cache hits and misses alternating. snippet: 
```
[1772003651] api_key=acct-987 cache_key=prefix:project-123 hit=model_variant=open-embed-2 dim=1536
[1772003780] api_key=acct-987 cache_key=prefix:project-123 hit=model_variant=open-embed-1 dim=1024
[1772003905] api_key=acct-987 miss cache_lookup=prefix:project-123 -> backend_compute
```
Maya Patel: oh yeah that's definitive. cache_key didn't include model name so both variants wrote under same key. race between warm batches could flip stored vector length.
Kevin O'Reilly: batching makes this worse — large prefetched batches populated by whichever model was warm first. Under load, we saw flip-flop where worker A serving open-embed-2 writes cache, then worker B serving open-embed-1 overwrites it.
Alex Chen: customer impacted: their downstream PCA/ann index breaks on dim mismatch, causing noisy errors. they flagged as production incident.
Billing Bot: flagged unusual spike in compute during the window 1772003500-1772004500 (customers retried due to mismatch). estimated extra tokens: 1.2M -> potential $120 extra.
Maya Patel: immediate mitigation options: 1) force cache purge for that prefix for the customer 2) disable prefix-serving optimization 3) roll back deploy that removed model from key.
Kevin O'Reilly: I pushed a small hotfix to restore model+quant in cache key if `prefix` present (PR 9483). would like to toggle via feature flag.
SRE Oncall: rolled feature-flag off for embed-cache change at 1772004550. monitoring now shows consistent dims in subsequent requests.
Alex Chen: relayed to customer: purged their prefix cache and toggled flag; asked them to stop retries for 10 minutes.
Customer (via support ticket): confirmed dims are stable now. thanks. :tada:
Maya Patel: follow-ups: - create migration/audit to detect prefix reuse across models (alert) - add validation: if a cache hit returns vector with unexpected dim, treat as miss and recompute + log an event with model mismatch. - update docs: warn that `prefix` must be unique per model family or we namespace automatically.
Kevin O'Reilly: I'll add the strict mismatched-dim fallback (treat as miss) and a counter metric `emb_cache.dim_mismatch_count`.
Billing Bot: created billing adjustment draft for customer showing retried compute and proposed credit.
Alex Chen: thanks everyone. putting postmortem notes in #postmortems and pinging account exec to handle CS escalation. closing thread when postmortem link created.
SRE Oncall: bringing up a small test to simulate cross-model prefix overwrite in staging. will link results.
Kevin O'Reilly: PR merged and flag gated. will schedule proper rollback if any weirdness.
Alex Chen: final status - resolved for customer, action items assigned: Kevin (cache key fix + metric), Maya (docs + alert), SRE Oncall (staging test + monitor), Billing (credit).
